title: AES information document for professional audio — Application of connectors, concentric phone plugs and jacks
abstract: Defines standardized allocations, contacts, and mating practices for concentric phone plugs and jacks (1/4 inch, 6.35 mm, 3.5 mm) used in professional balanced and unbalanced audio systems.

key_definitions.jack: Female concentric connector, usually fixed to equipment or connector panel.
key_definitions.plug: Male concentric connector, usually terminating a free cable.
key_definitions.TRS_plug: 3-contact concentric plug where the contacts are identified as Tip, Ring, and Sleeve.
key_definitions.TS_plug: 2-contact concentric plug where the contacts are identified as Tip and Sleeve.
key_definitions.IEC_plug: 2-contact or 3-contact concentric plug compliant with IEC 60603-11.
key_definitions.B_gauge_plug: 6.35 mm (nominal sleeve diameter) 3-contact concentric plug identified in Standard Sheet 12 of IEC 61602 (broadcast patch fields).
key_definitions.MIL_plug: 6.35 mm 3-contact concentric plug identified in US military specification PJ-051.

interoperability_and_hazards.ts_in_trs_hazard: When a monophonic 2-contact TS plug is inserted into a balanced TRS jack, the long sleeve shorts the Ring contact to Sleeve (Ground). In active cross-coupled or ground-referenced push-pull driver topologies, this dead-shorts an active op-amp output to ground, causing excessive thermal stress, output stage clipping, and increased distortion.
interoperability_and_hazards.insertion_shorting: Concentric plugs momentarily short adjacent contacts (Tip to Ring or Ring to Sleeve) during physical insertion and withdrawal. Equipment must include current limiting (series output resistance >= 50 Ω) and DC blocking to prevent internal amplifier damage.

relevance_to_balanced_audio: Specifies 1/4" TRS balanced patchbay and line I/O interconnects, highlighting critical differences between active floating versus ground-referenced op-amp drivers when mated with unbalanced cabling.
